The first pathway links Crassostreaxanthin B to the Glucagon receptor, which is targeted by Schisandilactone G, and then to HEp-2. The second pathway connects Crassostreaxanthin B to the Glucagon receptor, which is targeted by 16-Propoxystrychnine, also leading to HEp-2. The third pathway involves Crassostreaxanthin B targeting Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1, which is targeted by Methyl 4-methylhexanoate, and again leading to HEp-2. These pathways suggest that Crassostreaxanthin B may act through different molecular mechanisms to influence HEp-2, potentially through the activation of signaling pathways or the modulation of cellular processes. The consistent involvement of HEp-2 in all three pathways indicates a possible role in the cellular response to Crassostreaxanthin B, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
